title: H^2 of a torsion sheaf on an affine curve vanishes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ an affine curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (an affine scheme, separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension at most one; it may be empty, disconnected, singular or have zero-dimensional components). For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $H^2(C_{\Et},F)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves) (2) in degree 2; Lean: WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/CohomologicalDimension.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine, lines 386-395 (reduction AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine_of_forall, sorry-free, to smooth affine connected curves, AlgebraicGeometry.IsConnectedCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine_of_smooth)

proof.text: *Reduction to smooth affine connected curves.* By [lem-sc-affine-h2-smooth-reduction], applied to the affine curve $C$ and the torsion sheaf $F$, it suffices to prove: for every connected curve $C'$ over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (nonempty, connected, of dimension one) which is smooth over $k$ and an affine scheme, and every torsion abelian sheaf $F'$ on $C'_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $H^2(C'_{\Et},F')=0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Fix such $C'$ and $F'$ for steps 2-4.

source.place: unit sk-prop-cd, Step 1 (reduce to a smooth integral curve); Lean WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/CohomologicalDimension.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine, lines 386-395 (application of subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine_of_forall)

proof.text: *$C'$ is integral.* $C'$ is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian ($k$ is a field, hence a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), so $C'$ is Noetherian, in particular locally Noetherian, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. $C'$ is a smooth curve over $k$, so every local ring $\mathcal O_{C',P}$ is a regular local ring by [lem-sc-smooth-regular]; hence $C'$ is a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. As a connected curve, $C'$ is nonempty and connected, so $C'$ is integral by [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. It is separated over $k$ (it is a curve), so $C'$ is a smooth integral separated, affine and connected curve over $k$; let $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}k(C')\to C'$ be its generic point, $k(C')$ its function field [def-sc-function-field].

source.place: Tags 0569 and 033N (regular, hence normal, locally Noetherian and connected implies integral); Lean WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/CohomologicalDimension.lean, AlgebraicGeometry.IsConnectedCurve.subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine_of_smooth, lines 357-378, first six lines (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian, IsRegular.of_smooth, IsRegular.irreducibleSpace, isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced)

proof.text: *Passage to the generic point.* By [lem-sc-generic-cohomology-comparison] applied to the smooth integral separated curve $C'$, the torsion sheaf $F'$ and $q=2$, the unit $F'\to\eta_*\eta^{-1}F'$ of the adjunction $\eta^{-1}\dashv\eta_*$ ([def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]) induces an isomorphism $H^2(C'_{\Et},F')\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(C'_{\Et},\eta_*\eta^{-1}F')$.

source.place: unit sk-prop-cd, Step 2 (push to the generic point: $H^q(C,F)\cong H^q(C,\eta_*M)$ for $q\ge2$); Lean WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Curve/CohomologicalDimension.lean, subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine_of_smooth, via AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve.isIso_functorH_map_unit_fromSpecFunctionField (lines 311-325)

proof.text: *Vanishing at the generic point; conclusion.* $M=\eta^{-1}F'$ is a torsion abelian sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k(C')_{\Et}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion] (torsion in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], which agrees with that of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]: every local section is locally killed by a positive integer). By [lem-sc-affine-generic-second], applied to the smooth integral affine connected curve $C'$ of step 2 and to $M$, $H^2(C'_{\Et},\eta_*M)=0$. By step 3, $H^2(C'_{\Et},F')\cong H^2(C'_{\Et},\eta_*M)=0$. This is the hypothesis of step 1 for $C'$ and $F'$, so $H^2(C_{\Et},F)=0$.
